disagreements.topic: When Kyber ships, and whether the Kyber midplane risk hits inside the horizon
disagreements.positions: agent_1, agent_3 and agent_5 treat Kyber as shipping with Rubin Ultra in 2H27, inside the horizon, and add bear weight or a multiple haircut. agent_4 says Kyber slipped to 2028, so Rubin Ultra in 2027 stays on Oberon copper, APH is a relative beneficiary, and the risk is mostly 2028+. agent_2 says APH licenses its VR Ultra backplane IP to FIT and TE, which means share dilution rather than outright loss.
disagreements.resolution: Partly settled. SemiAnalysis did report on 2026-07-06 that Kyber NVL144 slips more than 12 months to 2028 on midplane PCB manufacturability. Several outlets carried it (DCD, Seeking Alpha, TheNextWeb), but Nvidia replied that its 'roadmap is intact', so the timing is not confirmed. The 'relative beneficiary' framing is not supported by the price action: APH fell 4.9% on 2026-07-07 (83.41 to 79.31) while SPY fell 0.5%. The Edgewater claims check out word for word in the 2026-09-30 report by named analyst Dennis Reed: APH is expected to license VR Ultra backplane IP to FIT and TE at Nvidia's request, is lead designer on the TPU9i cabled backplane (more than $750 per TPU vs $300-350), and has about 50-week fiber lead times. Net: the Kyber hit is more likely dilution and pushed toward 2028 than outright loss in 2027, and both the GF report and the delay news are already in the price. This argues against adding more left-tail mass on top of what the agents now carry. It does not justify removing any.
disagreements.evidence: SemiAnalysis via DCD, Seeking Alpha, TheNextWeb and Futu (2026-07-06); Nvidia denial via Wccftech and Benzinga (2026-07-07); Twelve Data APH and SPY closes; passive-components.eu Edgewater channel checks (2026-09-30).

one_month_reasoning: Q3 results come on Oct 28 (call at 1 PM ET), with the FOMC decision the same day (Kalshi: 28% chance of a hike) and hyperscaler capex prints in the last week of October. The window ends with the Oct 30 close. A beat is likely, but the verified history (+3.6%, -12.2%, +3.2%, +4.5%) shows a soft Q4 guide can drive a sharp drop. The five round-2 models are now independent and close together, so I use their mean (P>=85.67 = 0.521).
confidence_reason: My searches confirmed the Kyber delay report (disputed by Nvidia), the Edgewater licensing and TPU9i claims, the Kalshi hike odds and the earnings date. Those findings push in opposite directions: the Kyber news trims the left tail, the hawkish Fed weighs on the multiple. None of them settles a disagreement enough to move the ladder away from the mean of the forecasters.
thesis_break_reason: A close below $59 would break the 2026 closing floor ($59.58 on Mar 30, $59.60 on May 19) and the $59.01 intraday low. That is about 18x 2027 consensus EPS of $3.29. Both earlier tests came on rotation or de-rating while estimates rose. A third break would most likely mean estimates are being cut: datacom book-to-bill below 1, a hyperscaler capex cut, or confirmed loss of Nvidia/TPU backplane content without an offset.
key_drivers: AI datacom momentum: 43% of sales and +63% organic in Q2-26 on a 1.23 book-to-bill. The Q3 guide is $9.3-9.4B and $0.70-0.71 post-split EPS (8-K). Sept channel checks (Edgewater) show connector book-to-bill of 1.2-1.3x and about 50-week fiber lead times.

2028 hyperscaler capex growth slows sharply (Goldman +12%, Morgan Stanley +14%, UBS +6%), and the stock will be priced on 2028 EPS by Oct 2027. That supports roughly 12-13% EPS growth and a 24-24.5x multiple, which puts fair value near spot.

Nvidia rack content: GF says FIT may be the major Kyber midplane supplier. SemiAnalysis says Kyber slipped to 2028 (Nvidia disputes this). Edgewater says APH licenses the VR Ultra backplane IP and leads TPU9i cabled-backplane design. The likely outcome is dilution in 2028, not a loss in 2027.
Rates: Kalshi prices a 70% chance of a December hike and 40% in January, a headwind for a 26x forward multiple that most agents ignore.
Event asymmetry: the Jan-26 beat sold off 12%, and the stock fell 20% in three weeks after Q1. 1-year realized vol is about 46%, so the fat tails are real.

fair_value.reason: The agents' fair values are 89.5, 90, 85.5, 88.6 and 89.5 (mean 88.6). All share 2.578B post-split diluted shares, 2027 EPS of $3.25-3.29, 12-13% growth into 2028, and a 24-24.5x multiple. I use NTM EPS of about $3.67 x 24.25x = $89. agent_3's extra discount for the 2028 capex cliff and Kyber is partly offset by the verified Edgewater evidence (licensing rather than outright loss, TPU9i content of more than $750 per TPU). The hawkish Fed keeps me from going above $89.

summary: The five round-2 forecasts have converged: median about $86, fair values $85.5-90, thesis breaks $58-60. They share the same facts: strong AI datacom orders, about 26x 2027 EPS, and a sharp 2028 capex slowdown. My fact-checks confirmed that Kyber was reported delayed to 2028 (Nvidia disputes it) and that APH is licensing its backplane IP and leading the TPU9i design, which makes the GF Foxconn report look like dilution in 2028 rather than a loss in 2027. They also confirmed a hawkish Fed (Kalshi: 70% chance of a December hike) that most agents ignore. These offset, so I keep the mean ladder (P>=86 = 0.516) with low confidence. Fair value is $89 and the thesis break $59. Expect a roughly flat, fat-tailed year that swings on the Oct 28 print and 2027 capex budgets.
